newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to hold debate on pension funds on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: France to hold debate on pension funds on Thursday.

text.p: The French government, keen to introduce pension funds quickly to France, was working out last-minute details on its proposals ahead of a parliamentary debate on Thursday designed to lay the legal framework for such retirement savings schemes.

Unlike Britain and the United States, where pension funds are huge stock market players, France depends on a system of universal pensions where the cost of paying pensioners is levied from the wages of today's workforce.
It has spent years discussing how such funds should be set up to complement the existing system, running at times into accusations from unions of privatising the welfare system.
Thursday's debate looks set to be the government's best chance yet of getting a bill on pension funds on the rails.
The debate, due to start at 1400 GMT, will be based on proposals drawn up by 1994 by then parliamentary deputies Jacques Barrot, Charles Millon and Jean-Pierre Thomas.
The government is currently holding talks with parliamentarians to agree amendments to this bill.
Government officials declined comment on the details of the talks and on the government's planned amendments.
But officials have said previously the pension funds are expected to be set up through an agreement between employers and employees and managed independently.
These are expected to have to follow European Union rules which prevent countries from imposing a legal requirement on pension funds to invest a minimum of their assets in shares.
The draft parliamentary law submitted two years ago had originally foreseen fixing a minimum for investment in shares, including in the company making contributions to the fund.
